reason: Two rendering facts were found on screen this episode and each cost a fix: the Fabric window only gets GL 3.2 from vanilla, and LOD faces ignored the night. Both belong to the LOD renderer class of work, with the open visual gaps recorded so the next session does not rediscover them.

The renderer skill lacks the frame-cost, flicker and A/B rules the E.3 to E.5 work established, and its known-gaps list still points at E.5, which is closed. The E.7 visual pass now owns those gaps (user remarks on leaves and water).

Two-frame agreement before applying a detail value is a non-obvious fix that was verified on NeoForge (first stat line went from 438 freed to 131 freed). Also corrects the stale default of 4 px (ADR-024 moved it to 8 px) in the same bullet, so the skill no longer contradicts the ADR.

User explicitly asked that the distance at which textures stop be selectable rather than fixed; this is a durable product preference for any future LOD visual threshold. Records the textures command and default so the skill matches ADR-025.
Reconcile: the old sky-brightness rule (getSkyDarken) is contradicted by the lightmap rule added in aa6bebe; the stale line would keep steering the next session toward the removed approach.

The user chose max-quality defaults when the measured cost was negligible and deferred the trade-off to the in-game settings screen; the skill only said "user choice" and did not state the default policy.

The AO line describes the pre-fix state (levels 0-1 only, neighbors counted as open). Commit 1084a20 replaced it; leaving it would make the next session reintroduce the border lines and the ring. Reconciles the old statement.

The before/after diff is what isolated the AO border lines to section edges. It is a reusable way to localize shader seams and it is not written down. Amplified-diff check gives a numeric confirmation instead of eyeballing.

Fluid top height rule (8/9 on every level, in blocks after the fill on coarse levels) was decided and verified this episode, but only recorded in the triage skill. The renderer skill owns the shader and height rules, so the rule belongs here, and the mismatch symptom is the one a future renderer edit would reintroduce.
Biome blending design (per-fragment tint, SSBO layout, vanilla option mirroring) was built this episode and is not documented in the renderer skill.
User stated the rule explicitly: follow vanilla's config; if the vanilla option is off, do nothing. Not yet in the renderer skill.

The dimension fog setting and its two modes are a durable rendering rule that the renderer skill does not state. Its behaviour was checked in the Nether and the user asked what Pushed Back does to the fog.

The episode added an opaque mask material that hides preview faces toward real terrain; the renderer must drop its quads before the opaque/translucent split. This is a renderer invariant a future session editing LodRenderer or MaterialColors must know.
